National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
238 AM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Rain chances and amounts are trending higher for late Sunday and 
early Monday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. A robust low pressure system will continue to impact the
region today and tonight, with frequent wind gusts strong
enough to bring down temporary outdoor structures such as tents
and holiday decorations, and possibly produce isolated power
outages. Widespread rainfall will taper off later this morning
and afternoon.
2. Gusty winds redevelop this afternoon and continue through
Friday. Light wintry precipitation is anticipated near the
Tennessee border tonight and Friday, however no significant
accumulations are expected. Warmer for the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: A robust low pressure system will continue to impact 
the region today and tonight, with frequent wind gusts strong enough 
to bring down temporary outdoor structures such as tents and holiday 
decorations, and possibly produce isolated power outages. Widespread 
rainfall will taper off later this morning and afternoon.

The near-term fcst remains mostly unchanged for Thanksgiving day, 
with a strong low pressure system deepening and tracking northward 
towards the Carolina Coast. The low will move onshore later this 
morning and eventually lift north of the Carolinas later tonight 
and into Friday. As the low tracks east of the Piedmont this morning, 
the pressure gradient temporarily relaxes allowing gusts to drop off 
substantially. The current Wind Advisory is still set to expire at 
10 AM this morning. If winds/gusts weaken enough before then, we may 
cancel the Advisory before 10 AM. We also remain in a Marginal Risk 
for excessive rain thru mid-morning, but the likelihood of additional 
significant rain across our region between now and then appears minimal 
at best. Some localized, poor drainage flooding could still occur if 
storm drains get clogged by leaves, but that's about it.


Key message 2: Gusty winds redevelop this afternoon and continue
through Friday. Light wintry precipitation is anticipated near 
the Tennessee border tonight and Friday, however no significant 
accumulations are expected. Warmer for the weekend.

As the sfc low pulls away to the north later today, the pressure 
gradient will tighten again but with winds aloft from the SW. These 
winds should mix down underneath a subsidence inversion, although 
they are not expected to be as strong as the first round of gusty 
winds have been. We can expect frequent gusts thru tonight with 
strong cold advection, and more gusts thru the day on Friday with 
speeds tapering off Friday evening. Overall, wind gusts are still 
expected to top out in the 25 to 35 mph range, and thus remain below 
Advisory speeds. Unless fcst speeds trend upward, an extension of the 
current Wind Advisory or the issuance of a new one is not planned at 
this time. With regards to precipitation, colder air aloft associated 
with the upper low moving NE up the TN valley will create a changeover 
from rain to snow showers with the expected wrap-around precip along 
the NC/TN border this evening. The movement of the upper low should 
help keep the low-level flow more WLY or WSWLY which is less-than-
favorable for upslope forcing away from portions of the Smokies, which 
is a limiting factor. As a result, the potential for snow accumulations 
still appears minimal. Most locations near the TN border will probably 
get less than an inch, with some isolated 1 to 3" possible. Locations 
east of the spine will likely remain dry. Temperatures will remain cool 
on Friday with highs roughly 10 degrees below normal.

The rest of the weekend looks relatively benign. Sfc high pressure 
moves back over the Southeast which supports a nice warm-up back to 
near-normal temps. A strong upper shortwave is expected to move out 
across the Plains Saturday night and Sunday which will help generate 
another strong sfc low that moves NE across the Midwest and lower Great 
Lakes Sunday into Monday morning. This system will push a cold front 
across our area Sunday night and into early Monday. The latest model 
guidance appears to be increasing the amount moisture return ahead of 
the front, and as a result, precip chances and amounts have trended 
higher with this fcst. Nonetheless, excessive QPF across our fcst area 
looks pretty unlikely at this time. Dry high pressure spreads back over 
the Southeast in the wake of the front, with temperatures near normal 
from Monday onward.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: LLWS remains a concern at KAVL and KHKY 
through 10Z but elsewhere LLWS should remain above 3000 ft AGL. Very 
gusty NE winds will continue through daybreak before a brief lull in 
gusts develops late this morning into early this afternoon. Winds 
turn SW this afternoon while becoming gusty again with gusts 
lingering into tonight. Gusts will mostly range from 20-30+ kts 
through the period outside of the brief lull. IFR to MVFR cig and 
vsby restrictions are noted across the terminals this morning as is -
RA. IFR cigs becoming more widespread through daybreak and should 
stick around through early this evening. -RA will stick around 
through at least daybreak, possibly lingering through mid-morning 
east of the mountains. KAVL should see -RA linger through at least 
the late morning hours. MVFR to IFR vsbys will stick around most of 
the day before lifting to VFR levels late afternoon/early evening. 
Cigs may lift to MVFR towards the end of the period but confidence 
is low so maintained IFR through the end of the 06Z TAF period for 
now. Will reevaluate this for the 12Z TAFs. 

Outlook: A pesky low VFR to high-end MVFR stratocu deck may linger 
into Friday. Gusty west to southwest winds will also linger into 
Friday night. Dry and VFR returns briefly on Saturday before a cold 
front brings a brief shot of rain and associated restrictions Sunday 
afternoon into Sunday night.
